text:
Charlie Coyle might be the unluckiest good player in the league right now. With him on the ice at five on five, Columbus has taken 57% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances, 13 points better than when he sits. That's a top-line impact. And yet the Blue Jackets have scored 11 fewer goals than those chances deserved with him out there, the biggest gap on this list by a distance.

His own line carries the same story. He has 15 points in 22 games and four goals on 6.3 expected, shooting 8.2% against a league norm of 13.5. Our wins-added measure has him 451st of 560, which tells you how cruel the bounces have been, not how he's played. He's at 20 minutes a night and climbing.

Evolving-Hockey had him 58th among forwards last season, with the caveat that strong teammates flattered his on-ice numbers. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his shot assists in the 90th percentile. He scored on a breakaway in New Jersey on Monday. If you're looking for a player whose results should catch up to his work, start here.
